Mossy Forest Feature Selection

Source: R/mf_fit.R
mf.Rd

Runs the Mossy Forest algorithm.

Usage

mf(
  X,
  y,
  module_membership,
  screen_params = screen_control(),
  select_params = select_control(),
  final_ntree = 500L,
  nodesize = NULL,
  num_processors = 1L,
  max_modsize = 5000L,
  verbose = 1L,
  seed = as.integer(Sys.time()),
  compute_interactions = TRUE,
  backend = "python",
  r_shap = "permutation"
)

Arguments

X

A data frame where each column is a feature.

y

Response vector (numeric for regression, factor for classification).

module_membership

A named character vector assigning each feature in X to a module. Names must match colnames(X). Modules named in select_control(unassigned_modules) form the unassigned pool, which is selected with its own elbow based threshold; all other modules use pi_thr.

screen_params

Screening parameters. See screen_control.

select_params

Selection parameters. See select_control.

final_ntree

Number of trees in the final random forest. Default 500.

nodesize

Minimum terminal node size. Defaults to 1 for classification and 5 for regression.

num_processors

Number of parallel threads for random forests. Default 1.

max_modsize

Maximum module size before blockwise pre reduction is applied (Python backend only). Default 5000.

verbose

Verbose level. 0 = silent; 1 = progress messages; 2 = detailed output. Default 1.

seed

Integer random seed for reproducibility. Defaults to current system time.

compute_interactions

Logical. If TRUE (default), the TreeSHAP interaction matrix is computed by the Python backend and by the pure R backend with r_shap = "treeshap". Set FALSE to skip it (faster); detect_interaction() and plot_potential_interactions() then have nothing to use. It has no effect with r_shap = "permutation", which never computes interactions.

backend

Computation backend. "python" (default) uses a Python scikit-learn / SHAP engine via reticulate and provides exact TreeSHAP values plus an interaction matrix. "R" uses a R ranger implementation, no Python installation required. Choose the final importance method with r_shap.

r_shap

Final SHAP / importance method used when backend = "R". Ignored for the Python backend. One of:

"permutation"

Ranger permutation variable importance (default). No extra packages needed. Returns a scalar VIM per feature; per observation SHAP values and SHAP based plots are unavailable.

"treeshap"

Exact TreeSHAP values via the R treeshap package. Requires treeshap. Also computes a \(p \times p\) interaction matrix, enabling detect_interaction() and plot_potential_interactions().

Value

An object of class mossy_forest.

References

Chernozhukov, V., Chetverikov, D., Demirer, M., Duflo, E., Hansen, C., Newey, W., & Robins, J. (2018). Double/cross-fit residualed machine learning for treatment and structural parameters. The Econometrics Journal, 21(1), C1-C68.

Lundberg, S. M., & Lee, S. I. (2017). A unified model for interpreting predictions. NeurIPS, 30.

Examples

# A small simulated regression problem with two modules of features
set.seed(1)
n <- 60
z <- rnorm(n)
X <- data.frame(a1 = z + rnorm(n, sd = 0.3), a2 = z + rnorm(n, sd = 0.3),
                a3 = z + rnorm(n, sd = 0.3), b1 = rnorm(n), b2 = rnorm(n),
                b3 = rnorm(n))
y <- z + rnorm(n, sd = 0.3)
membership <- c(a1 = "A", a2 = "A", a3 = "A", b1 = "B", b2 = "B", b3 = "B")

# The pure R backend needs no Python installation
fit <- mf(X, y, module_membership = membership,
          screen_params = screen_control(min_ntree = 50),
          select_params = select_control(n_reps = 10, min_ntree = 50),
          final_ntree = 50, backend = "R", verbose = 0, seed = 1)
print(fit)
#> --- Mossy Forest ---
#> Stable features selected: 2
#> 
#>   feature_name variable_importance module_membership
#> 1           a1              0.5034                 A
#> 2           a2              0.4403                 A
#> 
#> OOB prediction error: 0.1831
head(fit$final_SHAP)
#>   feature_name variable_importance module_membership
#> 1           a1              0.5034                 A
#> 2           a2              0.4403                 A

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# The Python backend (exact TreeSHAP) needs a configured Python environment
mf_setup(condaenv = "sfenv")
fit_py <- mf(X, y, module_membership = membership, backend = "python")
plot_importance(fit_py)
} # }
